items.q: The proteinuria of chronic tubulointerstitial disease is typically:
opts: Less than 2 g/day, with β₂ microglobulin in the urine
More than 3.5 g/day, in the nephrotic range, with oedema
Between 2 and 3 g/day, with RBC casts in the sediment
Absent in all cases, despite significant tubular damage
items.exp: Urine in CTID: proteinuria <2 g/day (β₂ microglobulin) — a tubular pattern, not nephrotic range. (Book p794)

items.q: The urinary sediment in CTID is described as:
items.exp: Urine in CTID: proteinuria <2 g/day (β₂ microglobulin) and inactive urinary sediments. (Book p794)

items.q: Match each CTID investigation with its finding — 1) Urine protein  2) Urinary sediment  3) RFT  4) USG … A) B/L small kidneys  B) <2 g/day with β₂ microglobulin  C) Deranged  D) Inactive
items.exp: CTID investigations: urine — proteinuria <2 g/day (β₂ microglobulin) with inactive sediments; RFT deranged; USG — bilateral small kidneys. (Book p794)

items.q: An ultrasound in a patient with CTID typically shows:
items.exp: USG in CTID: B/L small kidneys — the shrunken kidney of chronic tubulointerstitial fibrosis. (Book p794)

items.q: Fill up: The tubular protein marker raised in the urine of CTID is ______ microglobulin.
items.exp: Urine in CTID: proteinuria <2 g/day with β₂ microglobulin, indicating tubular proteinuria. (Book p794)

items.q: Regarding the pathophysiology of CKDu (CKD of unknown etiology), the book states:
opts: It is unknown, with theories proposed and no precipitating disease
It is caused by diabetes mellitus in all cases, with diabetic retinopathy
It is an inherited ciliopathy with multiple bilateral renal cysts on imaging
It is due to recurrent urinary tract infection with chronic pyelonephritis
items.exp: CKDu pathophysiology: unknown, theories proposed, and no precipitating disease. (Book p794)

items.q: CKDu is defined by the presence of a clear precipitating disease such as diabetes or hypertension.
opts: False — by definition no precipitating disease is present
True — diabetic nephropathy is the usual precipitant
False — CKDu always follows lithium therapy
items.exp: CKDu: pathophysiology unknown, theories proposed, and no precipitating disease. (Book p794)

items.q: All but one of the following are stated about CTID. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Nephrotic-range proteinuria with active urinary sediment
items.exp: CTID has subnephrotic proteinuria (<2 g/day) with inactive sediments and small kidneys. Nephrotic-range proteinuria with an active sediment indicates glomerular disease. (Book p794)
